methods.notes: The vendor app applies no scan filter of any kind -- no name, no service UUID -- it lists everything and the user picks; a paired controller is re-found by its stored address. "BT-912" and "BT-712" are the advertised device names the app reads back after a scan to colour its UI, i.e. the generic BLE module's model number, so any product built on the same module advertises one of them. Whether 0xFFB0 appears in the advertisement or only in the GATT table after connect is not established.

device.name: HOTWIRED 12V Bluetooth Heated Gear
device.notes: 12V motorcycle heated gear (jacket liner, pant liner, gloves, heating pad). Each garment has an independent BLE module. Gloves are paired in the UI. Two hardware variants detected: BT-912/BT-712 (both use ffb0-UUID family, with fallback support for fee0-UUID family on older modules). Protocol uses AA/55 framed 8-byte commands with echo-based acknowledgment. Frames carry NO checksum — an XOR helper exists in the app but is dead code (zero callers anywhere in the BLE path); bytes 3-6 are fixed-zero padding. No keep-alive heartbeat — write-with-retry pattern instead. Multi-device: the app manages up to 5 garment slots simultaneously (MyApplication.pairList) — each garment is an independent BLE peripheral with its own connection; nothing relays commands between garments. MAX HEAT LEVEL: 10 (0x0A). DO NOT EXCEED. WARNING: No BLE security — any nearby device can control the heat. WARNING: Burn/fire/electrical risk — see target.md safety section. ODM: MEC Addheat Co., Ltd. (addheat.com) — the "mec" in com.hotwired.mec. MEC Addheat's own first-party ADDHEAT app (com.anji.mec, updated 2025-08) is the same codebase white-labeled. The cloud backend app.ventureheat.com is still live (probed 2026-07-31), so this spec likely covers Venture Heat's Bluetooth HeatSync/AddHeat line and other MEC Addheat white-labels, not just HOTWIRED.

credentials.notes: No credentials exist anywhere in this protocol. That is the security finding, not an omission — see the warnings in `device.notes`.

factory_reset.effect: There is nothing to clear. The module holds no credential, no bond and no persisted configuration — heat level is commanded live and lost on power-down. Disconnecting the garment from 12V returns it to its power-on state, which is the only state it has.

methods.description: Connect over GATT to a garment module and write 8-byte AA/55 framed commands, confirming each by the echoed acknowledgment rather than a heartbeat.

steps.action: Connect the garment to 12V power so its module powers up and advertises.
Scan for advertisement name BT-912 or BT-712, or for service 0000ffb0; fall back to the fee0 service family for older modules.
Connect over GATT — no bonding is offered or required.
Write an 8-byte AA/55 framed command and wait for the echoed acknowledgment, retrying on no echo.
steps.expect: The module echoes the command frame back.

steps.action: For gloves, repeat for the second module and associate the two in client state; the hardware has no concept of a pair.

setup.notes:
Each garment is an independent BLE module with no provisioning of any kind: it advertises as BT-912 or BT-712 and accepts AA/55 framed commands from anything that connects. The "pairing" in the vendor app is a UI grouping — it associates the left and right glove modules in the app's own state so one slider drives both — and does not create a BLE bond or any binding on the hardware.
SAFETY: because there is no bond, key or authentication, any device in range can set the heat level. Treat the absence of setup as a hazard to surface to the user, not as a convenience. Never send a level above 10 (0x0A).

rejoin.notes: No network is joined and no bond is held, so a new client connects immediately once the previous one disconnects. This is also the failure mode: control is taken, not handed over.

variants.notes: Primary variant — blue UI progress bar
Secondary variant — same UUIDs, blue progress bar
Older revision using fee1/fee2 characteristics — yellow progress bar

entities.name: Battery Level
entities.notes: Binds the gauge bits of the CC status report's battery byte (the field's `mask` strips the present flag) and maps steps 0-4 to a nominal percent. AA echoes are excluded by the characteristic's `format_match`.

entities.name: Internal Temperature
entities.notes: Scale and offset unconfirmed — requires bench testing. The field is declared as whole degrees C as a hypothesis; see the format block. AA echoes are excluded by the characteristic's `format_match`.

types.description: Exact echo of last write command — serves as acknowledgment
types.name: command_echo

fields.description: Battery status byte. Parsed as binary: bits 0-3: charging flag (0=absent, non-zero=present) bits 5-7: level 0-4 mapping to 0/25/50/75/100% — as implemented (the app's control screen parses hexString2binaryString(...).substring(5); likely intended bits 4-7 — the app's off-by-one). Harmless either way: observed values only reach 4.
fields.name: battery

product_types.description: Gloves — paired zone, always synced together. If the two modules drift to different levels, the app syncs the LOWER one UP to match the higher one (safety-relevant: re-sync never lowers heat without the user).

safety.notes: The device firmware controls link-loss behavior — the app does not implement a keep-alive. A replacement client MUST implement its own fail-safe: - Loss of BLE link → command OFF or bounded timeout - Never auto-apply last level on reconnect without explicit user confirmation - "Off" must be reachable in one tap - Current commanded level must be displayed unambiguously at all times Stock-app behavior worth knowing: every ON toggle in the vendor app sends level 10 (full power) — the app's control screen calls control("01", …, 10). A replacement client should pick its own default-on level deliberately rather than copying that.

security.notes: Device uses connectGatt(autoConnect=false) with no bonding. Frames are plaintext — no encryption, no challenge-response. Cloud auth (mid/token headers) is for app features only, NOT BLE.

timing.notes: No periodic heartbeat — device echoes writes for ACK, sends unsolicited CC status reports

remaining_unknowns:
Which values of the battery byte's upper nibble mean "charging" as opposed to merely "present".
The internal temperature byte's unit and scale are a hypothesis (the app never displays it); bench-test against a thermometer before trusting the reading.

set_heat.description: Set heat on/off and level. Frame is [0xAA][status][level][0x00 x4][0x55] — worked examples from the stock app: OFF = AA00000000000055, ON level 1 = AA01010000000055, ON level 5 = AA01050000000055, ON level 10 = AA010A0000000055. The device echoes the exact frame back on the notify characteristic as its acknowledgment; the stock app retransmits after 3 s if no matching echo arrives.

status.description: Power state. Defaulted to ON so a level control sends only the level; level 0 turns the element off either way.

characteristics.name: Command Write
characteristics.notes: Primary write characteristic for BT-912/BT-712 modules. 8-byte frames: AA <STATUS> <LEVEL> 00 00 00 00 55. STATUS: 00=OFF, 01=ON. LEVEL: 00-0A (0-10 decimal). Device echoes frame back on notify characteristic as ACK. Also check fallback: 0000fee2-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb for older hardware revisions.

format.name: frame_type
format.notes: Only the status report is laid out below.

format.name: battery_status
format.notes: The low three bits of a packed byte: a five-step gauge, 0 = empty, 1 = 25 %, 2 = 50 %, 3 = 75 %, 4 = 100 %. The upper nibble (battery_present below) is a battery-present / charger flag, so the raw byte 0x14 reads "present, full".

format.name: battery_present
format.notes: Upper nibble of the battery byte: 0 = no battery shown, non-zero = present. The app treats it as a flag; which values mean "charging" is not established.

format.name: internal_temp_raw
format.notes: Device internal temperature. The app never displays it, so the unit and scale are inferred (0x20 = 32 reads plausibly as whole degrees C) — hypothesis until bench-tested.

format.name: control_state
format.notes: Unused by the app; meaning unknown.

format_match.notes: CC = status report. AA = echo of the last write, not decoded.

characteristics.name: Status Notify
characteristics.notes: Notifications provide two response types: Type 1 (AA prefix): Command echo acknowledgment. Type 2 (CC prefix): Status report with battery/temperature. CC format: CC <STATUS> <TEMPS> <BATTERY> <TEMP> <CONTROL>. Enable notifications via CCCD 00002902-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Connection order in the stock app: it issues readCharacteristic on ffb2 during service discovery BEFORE enabling notifications (per the app's BLE service). Also check fallback: 0000fee1-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. FRAME SELECTION: `format` describes the CC status report only, and `format_match` says so: an AA-prefixed notification is the echo of the last write and its bytes mean something else. Offsets are from the app's status parser (six bytes, one field each); the app decodes the battery byte as two bit groups and reads nothing from the temperature byte, so the temperature scaling is a hypothesis. Nothing here has been read back from hardware by this project.

characteristics.name: Command Write (fallback)
characteristics.notes: Alternate write characteristic for older hardware revision. Same frame format as ffb1.

characteristics.name: Status Notify (fallback)
characteristics.notes: Alternate notify characteristic for older hardware revision. Response format assumed same as ffb2 but UNPROVEN — the stock app enables notifications only on ffb2 and discards fee1 values without parsing (per the app's BLE service).

services.name: HOTWIRED Heated Gear Control Service (alt characteristics)
services.notes: Groups the fee1/fee2 fallback characteristics. Their parent service UUID is NOT known: the app never references a 0000fee0 service — it matches the fee1/fee2 characteristics while iterating ALL discovered services (per the app's BLE service). The duplicated ffb0 UUID here is a grouping placeholder, not a confirmed on-device service.
